title: Move Your Body
objectives: I can show and say jump, climb, crawl, stretch, and wiggle.
I can tell which part of my body moves in each action.
I can use a moving word to tell what I did on the playground.
rationale: Action verbs that children can act out build strong connections between a word and its movement, so they are among the easiest words to learn and remember. Jump, climb, and crawl move the whole body; stretch and wiggle move parts of it. Each of these verbs also takes -ed and -ing, which gives children their first look at word endings without teaching them as rules. The unit revisits under, behind, and loud through movement games, such as crawling under a table.

words.def: Push off the ground into the air.
words.ex: I jump over the small puddle.
words.ex2: The frog can jump onto a big rock.
words.nonExample: Sitting still on the floor is not jumping.

apps.writing: Draw a child who can jump.

cloze.s: The rabbit pushed off its back legs and began to ___ over the log.

cloze2.s: We bend our knees and then ___ high on the trampoline.

misuse.s: I jump by keeping both feet glued to the floor.
misuse.why: To jump you push your feet off the ground and go up in the air.

visual.alt: A frog and a kangaroo, two animals that jump.

words.def: Go up using your hands and feet.
words.ex: We climb the ladder to the slide.
words.ex2: A squirrel can climb a fence in a flash.
words.nonExample: Sliding down a hill is not climbing.

apps.academic: Climb the steps one at a time.
apps.writing: Draw a child who can climb.

cloze.s: To get to the top of the ladder, you must ___ one step at a time.

cloze2.s: The kitten wanted to ___ the curtain with its tiny claws.

misuse.s: We climb to the top of the slide by sliding down it.
misuse.why: To climb is to go up with your hands and feet; sliding goes down.

visual.alt: A person climbing up a ladder.

words.def: Move on your hands and knees.
words.ex: The baby likes to crawl on the rug.
words.ex2: We crawl through the soft tunnel.
words.nonExample: Running across the yard is not crawling.

apps.academic: Crawl like a bear to the door.

cloze.s: The baby is too small to walk, so she will ___ across the rug.

cloze2.s: A caterpillar will ___ slowly along the green leaf.

misuse.s: I crawl across the room by standing up and running.
misuse.why: To crawl you stay low on your hands and knees.

visual.alt: A baby and a caterpillar, both able to crawl.

words.def: Make your body long and reach out.
words.ex: I stretch my arms up high.
words.ex2: The cat will stretch after her long nap.
words.nonExample: Curling into a tiny ball is not stretching.

apps.academic: Stretch up high before we begin.

cloze.s: After sitting for a long time, I ___ my arms and legs.

cloze2.s: A rubber band can ___ longer when you pull both ends.

misuse.s: I stretch by pulling my arms in and curling into a tiny ball.
misuse.why: To stretch you reach out and make your body long.

visual.alt: A person and a cat both stretching their bodies long.

words.def: Move quickly from side to side.
words.ex2: The puppy will wiggle its tail.
words.nonExample: Standing very still is not wiggling.

cloze.s: The worm began to ___ in the dirt, moving from side to side.

cloze2.s: When the music played, we all began to ___ and dance.

misuse.s: I wiggle my fingers by holding my hand perfectly still.
misuse.why: To wiggle means to move; holding still is the opposite.

visual.alt: A worm and a puppy, both wiggling.

passage.title: Little Bear Wakes Up
paras: Little Bear wakes up and stretches his arms. He crawls out of the cave on all fours.
A big rock sits by the path. Bear wants to climb it, and he goes up one paw at a time.
At the top he jumps for joy. His tail wiggles and wiggles!

qs.q: Little Bear crawls out of the cave. How does he move?
qs.why: To crawl is to move low on hands and knees; the story says he goes out on all fours.

qs.q: What does Bear want to climb?
qs.why: A big rock sits by the path, and Bear wants to climb it.

qs.q: Why does Bear's tail wiggle at the end?
qs.why: He jumps for joy at the top, so his wiggling tail shows he is happy.

write.prompt: Pick one moving word from this unit. Show it with your body, then tell a partner or draw when you do it.

study.task: Act out each moving word. Then tell a partner what you did on the playground today, using one of the words.

words for moving parts of your body

When do you need to stretch?

teacher.overview: Children learn five action words by moving their bodies, then hear them in a short story about a bear cub and say them in short sentences. Every word is taught through movement; no reading or writing is needed.

notes.va.jump.v: Contrast jump with hop and with step: jump uses two feet and goes up. Have children jump softly and loudly to review loud and quiet. Keep space clear for safety.
notes.va.climb.v: Use a low climber or steps and keep safety first. Climb means going up with hands and feet; sliding down is the opposite. Do not ask children to climb on classroom furniture.
notes.va.crawl.v: Do a bear crawl under a table to review under and behind. Crawl is low and slow on hands and knees; children may confuse it with creep or walk on all fours.
notes.va.stretch.v: Teach as reaching out long, not just up. Pair stretch with a calm breath. A rubber band can also stretch; show it to link the body meaning to the object meaning.
notes.va.wiggle.v: Wiggle is small quick moves from side to side. Children may know squirm; accept it as a near synonym. Wiggle fingers, toes, and a loose tooth for friendly examples.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I want to move like a bear cub. First I stretch my arms out long. Now I get down low and crawl on my hands and knees. Say it with me: I crawl. Now I wiggle my toes.'
discuss: Which move can you do under a table? Show me.
Which move uses your whole body?
misconceptions: Jump and hop mean exactly the same thing.
Climb means any way of going up, including a lift.
extend: Play Simon Says using the five words, with one child as leader.
Make a class book: each child draws one action and says the word with a friend.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit under, behind, and loud by giving movement directions, such as crawl under the table or jump quietly. Use jump and stretch again in unit 7 with opposites, and climb in unit 9 for the compound words.

wida.oral: Partner A acts out one moving word without speaking. Partner B says the word and a sentence, such as 'You jump like a frog.' Then they switch.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (saltar, trepar, gatear, estirar, menear) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; gatear is specific to babies and arrastrarse may fit other crawling, and trepar and subir both fit climb.
Sense boundary: stretch is taught as a body action (reach out long); the object sense, as in a rubber band, appears only in one example.
Sense boundary: crawl is taught as moving on hands and knees; the swimming crawl is left out.
The scope names morph-productive for these verbs (-ed and -ing); the unit keeps study.focus none and does not teach endings as rules.
